encounters.title: Strangers from the Void
encounters.description: Sensors detect a vessel that defies all known physics. It shimmers into existence—a crystalline lattice rather than a hull. The being on screen is a mass of shifting light, speaking directly into Aristotle's mind. "We observe your struggle with the lower lifeforms. We offer... elevation. At a cost."

choices.text: "Whatever gives us the edge. What do you need?"

outcome.description: The aliens integrate their tech into your ships. The Corsairs become practically ethereal, but the physical toll on the crew is terrifying.

choices.text: "I don't make deals with things I can't look in the eye. Leave our sector."

outcome.description: The entity pulses a shade of angry crimson and vanishes. The more traditional factions respect your decision to refuse the supernatural.

choices.text: Attempt to steal their technology during the parley without making a deal.

outcome.description: It goes disastrously wrong. The aliens don't use technology; they ARE the technology. Several of your science team are vaporised.

encounters.title: A Quiet Meeting
encounters.description: Commander Dave sends a secure, unencrypted channel request. Not an ambush. A meeting. Neutral ground, a derelict station on the fringe.

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: Dave is already seated when you arrive, paws folded on the rusted table. No guards. No weapons visible. He looks older than you remember.

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "Sit down, Aristotle. I didn't drag us both to this heap of scrap for posturing."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Lovely place you've picked. Very romantic. Is that rust or blood on the walls?"

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "Both, probably. Listen to me carefully. The Sovereigns are moving. Lions from the core, Wolves from the rim. They don't care about our little war. They want the crystals, and they will grind us both to dust to get them."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Us both? That's generous. Last I checked, you were the one blockading my trade routes."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "And last I checked, you were the one selling fuel to anyone with coin, including factions that would burn the League to cinders." Dave's jaw tightens. "But that's yesterday's argument. The Sovereigns are tomorrow's problem. And tomorrow is coming fast."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "So what are you proposing, Commander? That we hold paws and sing together?"

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "I'm proposing that we stop being useful idiots. Every time we fight each other, the Sovereigns get stronger. They're playing us, Aristotle. Both of us." He leans forward. "I need to know if there's anything behind that grin of yours besides ego."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Aristotle's grin flickers. For a fraction of a second, something real shows through. Then the mask is back.

choices.text: "Then let's stop fighting each other. We pool our intelligence, split the crystals. Temporary ceasefire, mutual benefit."

outcome.description: Dave slowly nods. "A temporary arrangement. Until the real threat is dealt with." A bizarre, fragile peace is formed.

choices.text: "I don't need your help, Dave. I've built an empire from nothing. I can defend it from everything."

outcome.description: Dave sighs, looking tired. "Pride goeth before destruction, cat. Expect no mercy when the end comes."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: Dave extends a paw across the table. It is not a friendly gesture. It is a contract. "Temporary. Until the Sovereigns are dealt with. Then we renegotiate."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Temporary. Obviously." Aristotle takes the paw. The grip is firm on both sides. Neither trusts the other. Both need each other. It's the ugliest alliance in the multiverse.

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "I'll transmit League intelligence on Sovereign fleet movements. You share your crystal cache locations. Non-negotiable."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: Dave stands slowly. He buttons his coat with mechanical precision. "I came here because I thought you might surprise me. You didn't."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Don't let the airlock hit you on the way out, Commander."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "When the Sovereigns come for you—and they will—remember this moment. Remember I offered you a hand and you slapped it away." He turns and walks out without looking back.

encounters.title: The Master's Voice
encounters.description: The shadows on the bridge solidify. Death stands before you, having bypassed every lock, every guard, every alarm. He is not here to kill. He bows.

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: The temperature on the bridge drops ten degrees. Crew freeze at their stations. Death materializes from nothing, shadows pooling at his feet like spilled ink.

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "Captain Aristotle. I have tested your fleet. Your resolve. Your... resourcefulness." The purr is low, vibrating through the deck plates. "You have proven adequate."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Adequate? I've been losing sleep over you for two arcs and I get 'adequate'? I'm insulted."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "Insult is a luxury of the living, Captain. I deal in truths. And here is one: I did not come to you on my own initiative. I was sent." Death's eyes glow like dying embers. "My true masters wish to discuss the final disposition of the crystals."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Masters. The great and terrible Death has masters. Now that IS interesting." Aristotle circles him slowly. "So who holds your leash, shadow?"

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "Perceptive creatures guess. Fools demand answers. Which are you, Captain?" Death's form flickers, shadows dancing. "Tell me who you think I serve. I will confirm or deny nothing. But your guess will... shape what follows."

choices.text: "You work for the Lion Sovereign. I should have known. You're a lap cat after all."

outcome.description: Death purrs. "The Sovereign offers order. The chaotic distribution of crystals must end. We act as their unseen hand."

choices.text: "The Wolves of the Outer Rim. You're an anarchist wrapped in shadows."

outcome.description: Death chuckles, a dry, rattling sound. "The Sovereigns and the League are stagnant. The fire must be stoked. The crystals are the spark."

choices.text: "You don't work for anyone. You want the monopoly for yourself, you greedy ghost."

outcome.description: Death's eyes widen slightly. "You perceive clearly, Captain. Why serve a king when one can be a god?"

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: Death's purr deepens. "The Sovereign understands what you do not. Order is not the enemy of freedom. It is its foundation. The crystals must flow through proper channels."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Proper channels. You mean golden paws. Lion paws."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "Better a crown than a pirate's noose, Captain. Consider whose hand you would rather feed from." The shadows begin to recede. "We will speak again. When the time comes... choose wisely."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: A rattling chuckle fills the bridge. "The wolves understand hunger. The old orders are calcified. Brittle. The multiverse needs fire, not more rules."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Fire has a habit of burning the one who lights it, Death."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "Only if you stand too close. I never stand too close to anything, Captain. It is the secret to longevity." He dissolves into the darkness between the consoles. "The wolves send their regards. And their teeth."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: Death goes very still. The shadows around him freeze. Then his eyes widen, and for the first time, something like genuine emotion crosses that spectral face.

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "You perceive clearly, Captain. Dangerously clearly." The purr drops to a whisper. "Why serve a king when one can be a god? The crystals are not fuel. They are power. And power belongs to those bold enough to seize it."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Takes one to know one, I suppose. We're not so different, you and I."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "No, Captain. We are nothing alike. You hoard for profit. I hunger for something far older." The shadows swallow him whole. Only the echo of his purr remains, vibrating in the walls.

encounters.title: A Web of Deals
encounters.description: With the major players distracted, the smaller factions smell blood in the water. The Goblin scavengers and the isolated Fairy enclaves both offer you exclusive, highly illegal technology—but only if you betray the other to them.

choices.text: Arm the Goblins and give them the coordinates to the Fairy enclaves.

outcome.description: The scavengers swarm the graceful Fairy ships. Brutal, but effective. The scavengers give you advanced scrap-tech weapons.

choices.text: Provide the Fairies with crystal overchargers to wipe out the Goblin fleets.

outcome.description: The Fairy ships dance through the scavenger swarms, tearing them apart with pinpoint energy lances. The Fairies grant you powerful defensive shields.

choices.text: Take their money and do neither. Let them kill each other.

outcome.description: Both factions realize they've been played. They break off their war just long enough to put bounties on your head.
